content:
People will ask where your Core Group comes from. A friend, another church, a new believer, someone finding their way back. Those are real paths. Do not open all of them on the same week, and do not give each path a quota.

Begin with a sending nucleus. Gather a small group from one sending church, and ask that group to share the work of welcoming and developing the people who join later. After that group has committed, widen the invitation. The Core Group funnel stays the same for every person.

---

## Name one sending church

A sending church releases people to this plant, prays for the work, and stays in the conversation with you. If more than one church cares about the plant, choose the one that will actually do those things. Listing several churches is not a sending relationship.

If you do not have a sending church yet, ask a church that knows you to take the role before you widen invitations. Ask for a few people who will commit, not a crowd and not a budget promise. If that church says no, ask another church that knows your life and your doctrine. Do not skip the sequence because the first conversation was awkward, and do not invent a sending relationship to fill a blank.

The nucleus is small on purpose. It is not a percentage of the future Core Group, and it is not the whole sending congregation. A short list of people who will share the work is enough to begin. Some may move. Some may already live near the plant. Some may serve for a season and then return. Ask the sending church's pastors whom they would commend, then talk with those people yourself.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away."* — Acts 13:3 (LSB)
</Callout>

Ask for that kind of send-off. A quiet bulletin announcement is not the same thing.

---

## Run the same funnel for each person

The published funnel has no side door for people you already know. The path is still network, Vision Meeting, follow-up, and Core Group. Hold a Vision Meeting for the nucleus, even if the room is a living room. Follow up in person. Interview before anyone commits.

That interview is a dated judgment you make about maturity, gifts, chemistry, reasons for coming, and season of life. Write the date and what you decided. Everyfield can keep the interview you record. It does not make the judgment. It never decides calling, character, fitness, or spiritual health, and it does not certify a sending church or a nucleus.

Where someone came from supplies neither qualification nor commitment. Count a person in the adult Core Group only after a supported commitment is actually in place. A planning lunch, a group text, and a warm yes are not that commitment. Each adult needs their own. One person's yes does not cover a spouse.

<Callout type="important">
Familiarity is not an interview. If you would ask a stranger about reasons, season of life, and unresolved conflict, ask the person from the sending church the same things.
</Callout>

---

## Give the nucleus the welcome work

Shared ownership starts with this first group, not after you are large. Growing the Core Group is every member's work, with prayer and giving beside it. The nucleus also carries a charge that is easy to skip. They share responsibility for welcoming and developing people who were not in the sending church.

Say that before you widen invitations.

- Teach the 4 Pillars, and Worship, Walk, Work, and Witness, in ordinary words.
- At the next gathering, sit with someone who just arrived. Tell old stories so a new person can follow.
- Invite from local life, not only from the sending church directory.
- Stay with a newer believer through the first gatherings. Teaching the rhythms is not the same as leaving them at the edge.

| Charge | Do not skip |
| --- | --- |
| Invite, pray, and give | Leaving the invitations to the Senior Pastor |
| Welcome later members | Inside language and closed circles |
| Tell the truth in the interview | Treating a referral as a pass |

<Callout type="warning">
A nucleus can carry an insider culture into the new church. Inside jokes, meals that never add a chair, and decisions made in a side thread teach later members that they are visiting someone else's church. Name that when you see it. The plant is not a smaller copy of the sending church.
</Callout>

---

## Widen the invitation next

Once the nucleus has committed and taken the welcome charge, widen the ask. Friends, family, colleagues, neighbors, people from other churches, and people the nucleus knows in the plant's area. A personal invitation still does the work. A broad email is a weak substitute.

Include people unhappy with their current church, people new to faith, and people reconnecting with church. Same Vision Meeting. Same follow-up. Do not hold them until the Core Group feels mature enough, and do not speed them through because you want a different story. The interview still asks about reasons. Joining only to escape a conflict is a poor reason, wherever they came from.

If people from outside the sending church are already in conversation, finish their follow-up and interview. Do not drop them to restart the calendar. Still form the nucleus and give it the welcome work.

Do not assign percentages to sources. A quota pretends that source predicts maturity. It does not. A committed adult from a local relationship and a committed adult from the sending church count the same way. Neither counts before the commitment exists.

---

## Keep the two stories distinct

People who come from an existing church and people who come to faith are different stories. Transfer can still be real growth for a launch. It is not the same story as people who were far from Christ learning to follow Jesus. Ask the nucleus who nearby has no church, and who might be ready to hear the gospel. Invite those people.

Keep a plain note of where each person came from, for your review with a coach. Do not turn the note into a contest. Professions of faith and baptisms are not points. A Core Group that started in a sending church is not a failure. Tell the truth about the difference. Do not rank people by it.

<Callout type="tip">
At the next nucleus meeting, ask each person for two names from local life, not from the sending church directory. Pray for those names, then invite them to the next Vision Meeting. Review the invitations. Do not review a scoreboard.
</Callout>

---

## Work the conversations

Use this list with the sending church and with the nucleus. It is a plan for human conversations. Nothing in Everyfield grades the list, blocks a Vision Meeting, or decides who may be asked.

- [ ] Name the sending church and the pastors you will ask.
- [ ] Make a short list of people from that church for the nucleus.
- [ ] Hold a Vision Meeting for them, then follow up in person.
- [ ] Interview each person. Record the date and your judgment.
- [ ] Ask for a dated commitment before you count them in the Core Group.
- [ ] Tell the nucleus that welcoming and developing later members is their work.
- [ ] Then widen invitations to local relationships, other churches, new believers, and people reconnecting with church.
- [ ] Use the same follow-up and the same interview for every later person.

---

## Watch for these mistakes

Opening every network on week one and calling the crowd a nucleus. Start with the sending church, then widen.

Treating a pastor's commendation as a pass. Thank them for the referral, then interview.

Waiting to widen until the nucleus feels finished. After the commitment and the welcome charge, invite locally.

Letting the nucleus recruit only its own friends. That copies the sending church into a new room and leaves the plant thin where it meets.

Counting interested people before a supported commitment exists. The adult benchmark in Growing Your Core Group is a planning mark for this way of planting, not a universal grade of health.

Wording call: kept the backlog title, Where Your Core Group Comes From, because it names the question. The body answers only with the ruled sequence.
Wording call: a planter with no sending church asks a church that knows them to take that role before widening invitations, rather than skipping the sequence or inventing a relationship.
Wording call: small means a short list, not a number and not a source quota. No percentage mix.

Wording call: if people from outside the sending church are already in conversation, finish their follow-up and interview. Do not drop them to restart the calendar. Still form the nucleus and give it the welcome work.
Wording call: sort_order 6, after the five published articles in this section, so published order is unchanged.

Consistency: same funnel, interview, and commitment as The Core Group Funnel and Growing Your Core Group. People unhappy with their church may be invited, and joining only to escape a conflict is a poor reason. Source supplies neither qualification nor commitment. Adult count requires a supported commitment. Transfer and new-faith stories stay distinct without a contest. The adult benchmark remains a methodology planning mark, not a universal health grade. Software never judges calling, character, fitness, or spiritual health.
